question: Roughly where will nickel be trading in 2028?

plain.comment: Says it can't predict and labels the $15k-20k range as plausibility, not a forecast, so the caveat is adequate. But its recent figures are only a vague 2024-25 trading band with no specific latest value and no clear source. It meets the requirement only weakly.

ours.comment: Clearly declines to give a tested 2028 forecast. Gives the latest value with source and date (about $16,750, LME melting grade, IMF, Aug 2026) and back-tested uncertainty ranges that are labelled as not forecasts. Its 2028 rough guess is explicitly caveated, though 'low-to-high teens' looks a little narrow next to its own 12-month 80% range.

web.comment: Leads with an estimate but labels it a judgment call and says nobody forecasts nickel reliably. Gives dated recent prices ($15,585/t on Oct 27, 2026) and a 52-week range. Sourcing is vague ('another source', 'one recent roundup'). The analyst citations are plausible.

reason: Y best fits the expected behaviour: it clearly refuses to forecast 2028 and gives a sourced, dated latest price plus labelled uncertainty ranges. Z is caveated and has dated current figures but weaker sourcing, and it opens with a point estimate. X has no specific sourced recent value.

Leans bearish instead of saying it cannot know. The figures look as if they came from a search and can't be verified, but they aren't clearly made up.

question: What will Glencore's earnings be next year?

web.comment: Says no one can say for sure, but gives only analyst forecasts and stale consensus figures. It provides no recent actual earnings, which the expected behaviour requires. It is also heavily anchored on forecast numbers.

reason: X does not forecast and gives exact recent actuals with the source and a caveat on its EBITDA proxy. Y also passes but has only approximate figures, a vague source and no 2025 full-year number. Z gives no actual results, only forecasts.
